title: First Sino-Japanese War
summary: In 1894 Korea, unable to defeat the Tonghak rebels, called on China for help, and Japan sent troops too. The war that began in July was fought on land and sea: fighting spread from Korea over the Yalu into Manchuria, Japan's navy won the Battle of the Yellow Sea, and Japanese forces took Port Arthur, the Liaodong Peninsula and Weihaiwei. China sued for peace and in the Treaty of Shimonoseki, signed on 17 April 1895, ceded Taiwan and recognised Korea's independence. Japan emerged as a major power in East Asia.

uncertainty.note: Hostilities began with naval clashes at Pungdo on July 25, 1894; the conflict concluded with the signing of the Treaty of Shimonoseki on April 17, 1895.

as_recorded.value: Sino-Japanese War began in July 1894 and ended in China’s shattering defeat in April 1895

where.modern_name: Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan (site of the signing of the Treaty of Shimonoseki ending the war; major combat spanned Korea, the Yellow Sea, and the Liaodong Peninsula)

importance.justification: Overturned the East Asian order, began Japan's colonial empire and ended Chinese dominance over Korea (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: The peasant uprising prompted the Joseon government to request Chinese military intervention, leading Japan to deploy troops and triggering armed clashes.
The acquisition of Taiwan under the Treaty of Shimonoseki founded Japan's overseas territorial colonial empire.

beats.caption: Hostilities begin off the Korean coast, leading to rapid Japanese land advances through Pyongyang and into Manchuria.
China signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, ceding Taiwan to Japan and transforming the regional balance of power in East Asia.
